name: Do I need a building permit to remodel my bathroom?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a building permit to remodel my bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: Permits are generally required whenever a bathroom remodel involves structural changes, moving plumbing drain lines or supply pipes, adding new electrical outlets, or modifying exhaust venting. Surface-level cosmetic replacements, like changing a vanity in the exact same footprint or replacing a faucet, often do not require permits. For projects involving wall removal, tub-to-shower conversions that resize drain lines, or subfloor modifications, a licensed general contractor secures the proper residential permits through the local building department to ensure all work meets current safety codes and passes required inspections.
acceptedAnswer.description: Permits are typically required if your remodel alters plumbing pipes, electrical wiring, ventilation paths, or structural walls. Purely cosmetic updates usually do not.
